nodes.summary: For every variable $x$ and every CNF formula $\varphi$, the formula obtained from $\varphi$ by eliminating $x$ is satisfiable if and only if $\varphi$ is satisfiable.
nodes.title: Davis-Putnam elimination preserves satisfiability

nodes.summary: For every CNF formula $\varphi$, the Davis-Putnam procedure returns true on $\varphi$ if and only if $\varphi$ is satisfiable.
nodes.title: Correctness of the Davis-Putnam procedure

nodes.summary: Given a CNF formula $\varphi$, eliminate the variables that occur in $\varphi$ one after another, each exactly once, in the order of their first occurrence in $\varphi$, each elimination being applied to the result of the previous one. The procedure returns true if the resulting formula does not contain the empty clause, and false if it does.
nodes.title: The Davis-Putnam procedure

nodes.summary: Given a list $x_1, \dots, x_n$ of variables and a CNF formula $\varphi$, eliminate $x_1$ from $\varphi$, then $x_2$ from the result, and so on up to $x_n$. For the empty list the result is $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Successive elimination of a list of variables

nodes.summary:
Eliminating a variable $x$ from a CNF formula $\varphi$ gives the formula consisting of the clauses of $\varphi$ that contain neither $x$ nor $
eg x$, followed by the resolvents on $x$ of $C$ and $D$, for every clause $C$ of $\varphi$ that contains $x$ but not $
eg x$ and every clause $D$ of $\varphi$ that contains $
eg x$ but not $x$. Clauses containing both $x$ and $
eg x$ are dropped.
nodes.title: Davis-Putnam elimination of a variable

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a variable, $\varphi$ a CNF formula and $\sigma$ an assignment that satisfies the formula obtained from $\varphi$ by eliminating $x$. Then there is a truth value $b$ such that the assignment that agrees with $\sigma$ except that it sends $x$ to $b$ satisfies $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Completeness of a Davis-Putnam step

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a variable and let $C$ and $D$ be clauses such that $C$ does not contain $\neg x$ and $D$ does not contain $x$. Then no literal of the resolvent of $C$ and $D$ on $x$ has variable $x$.
nodes.title: Resolvents do not mention the resolved variable

nodes.summary: For a variable $x$ and a CNF formula $\varphi$, the formula consisting of the clauses of $\varphi$, in their order, that contain the literal $\neg x$ and do not contain the literal $x$.
nodes.title: Clauses containing a variable only negatively

nodes.summary: For a variable $x$ and a CNF formula $\varphi$, the formula consisting of the clauses of $\varphi$, in their order, that contain the literal $x$ and do not contain the literal $\neg x$.
nodes.title: Clauses containing a variable only positively

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a variable and $\varphi$ a CNF formula. Every assignment that satisfies $\varphi$ also satisfies the formula obtained from $\varphi$ by eliminating $x$.
nodes.title: Soundness of a Davis-Putnam step

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, the list of the variables occurring in the literals of $\varphi$, each listed exactly once, in order of first occurrence when the clauses of $\varphi$, and the literals within each clause, are read from left to right.
nodes.title: Variable list for Davis–Putnam elimination

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
